Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the two applicable skills: `fish-control-primitives` is explicitly required for the first architecture proposal, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` will structure the required rollout-evidence inspection before any policy edit. I’ll keep this to exactly one candidate and won’t consider it complete until both the candidate notes and reusable guidance are updated.

The workspace confirms that formal CFD must not be run here; evaluation happens after exit. I’m now anchoring the shelf consultation in the inherited evidence as required: first the full guidance and all sampled score/observation/metric summaries, then the shared prewarm and best-versus-failure keyframes. No architecture choice has been made yet.

All four sampled candidates are successful, so there is no sampled failure sheet to compare; I’m using the weakest successful prefill as the contrast and retaining the inherited naive-seed boundary-exit diagnosis only as logged historical failure evidence. The useful comparison is the best route/load example (`f878…`, 39.1104 release time, 54.19/754.87 RMS force/moment) against the prefill (`db159…`, 40.6450, 64.70/875.97). I’m inspecting those sheets now, including the common prewarm.

The visual comparison confirms self-propelled, target-directed motion: both successful sheets make the same early downward-left redirect and then enter the interacting wake corridor; the stronger candidate reaches on the same compact topology with lower excursions and loads. The inherited response-completion mechanism is now evaluated evidence: versus its assigned coherence parent it preserved the 39.1104 capture while reducing force/moment from 57.21/783.64 to 54.19/754.87 and command energy from 50060.7 to 50044.8, though both hard caps remain touched. Per `fish-control-primitives`, I’m now consulting the shelf references to choose a new mechanism-level test rather than another scalar threshold.

The selected test is one new semantic mechanism on the evaluated `f878…` carrier: an alignment-conditioned gait envelope. Full oscillator amplitude and steering remain exact whenever either persistent-route or current body-frame bearing still asks for correction; only during jointly aligned transit is carrier amplitude eased, and that extra easing fades near the existing approach regime so it does not compound terminal coasting. This follows the shelf’s closed-loop CPG amplitude-modulation invariant, while keeping all published gains, timings, phases, and routes out of the policy. I’m recording the required pre-edit diagnosis and transfer block now.

The candidate diff is clean: relative to the evaluated `f878…` carrier, it adds one parameter and one alignment-conditioned amplitude path; the sign-coherence selector, response-completion gate, steering biases, posterior lag, and large-error behavior remain unchanged. I’m now materializing the durable lesson from the completed `df084… → f878…` evidence—specifically, what improved and what did not—without treating this unevaluated candidate as evidence.

Both required files now carry substantive updates. I’m invoking the checks specified by `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` separately: first guidance semantics and parameter-schema validation, then the lightweight Julia include (not CFD), then the editable-boundary check. If Julia is absent as in the inherited worker, I’ll preserve that as an environment limitation and still complete every available static check.

Guidance semantics passed. The exact lightweight Julia command was invoked but cannot run because this image has no `julia` executable (exit 127); no CFD was attempted. I’m proceeding with the boundary and deterministic static/schema checks so the missing runtime is the only unresolved verification item.

The boundary check passed, and an independent deterministic schema audit found an exact 15/15 match between returned parameter fields and direct `params.FIELD` references. I’m adding these verification facts—and the unavailable Julia runtime—to the candidate notes, then I’ll rerun the semantic and boundary checks after that final provenance edit.

The final semantic and boundary reruns both pass. The only unavailable check is Julia execution itself; the candidate remains structurally/schema-valid and intentionally unevaluated by CFD. I’m doing one last completeness audit for nonempty files, the required bookshelf block, material parent-guidance difference, and the single candidate hash.

Produced exactly one candidate: an alignment-conditioned gait envelope layered onto the evaluated response-gated carrier.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:70)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:92)

Validation passed for guidance semantics, editable boundaries, completeness, and the 15/15 parameter schema. The lightweight Julia check was invoked but unavailable because `julia` is not installed. No formal CFD was run, per workspace contract.
